title: In Daniel 10 In What Ways Can We Apply Daniels Example Of Seeking God Through Prayer And Fasting In Our Own Lives
paragraphs: Learning from Daniel: Prayer, Fasting, and Seeking God (Daniel 10)

Daniel 10 offers a profound glimpse into the spiritual discipline of seeking God through prayer and fasting. Daniel, though living in exile and facing great challenges, remains steadfast in his devotion to God. This chapter not only records Daniel’s vision, but also his example as a man of prayer, humility, and perseverance. How can we, as believers today, apply Daniel’s example in our own walk with God?
The Context of Daniel’s Prayer and Fasting
Daniel 10 opens with Daniel deeply burdened by a vision concerning Israel. His response is recorded:

In those days I, Daniel, was mourning three whole weeks. I ate no pleasant bread, neither came flesh nor wine into my mouth, neither did I anoint myself at all, till three whole weeks were fulfilled. - Daniel 10:2-3 ASV
For three weeks, Daniel fasted and prayed, seeking understanding and intervention from God. This was not a casual prayer, but a season of deep mourning, humility, and earnest seeking.
Principles from Daniel’s Example
Persistent Prayer

Daniel did not give up after a brief prayer; he persisted for twenty-one days. This is echoed in the New Testament, where believers are encouraged to "pray without ceasing" (1 Thessalonians 5:17 ASV). Daniel’s persistence reminds us that seeking God often requires patience and endurance, especially when answers seem delayed.
Fasting as a Spiritual Discipline

Daniel’s fasting was an expression of humility and dependence on God. Fasting is not a way to manipulate God, but a way to focus our hearts, deny fleshly distractions, and seek God’s will. Jesus taught, "when ye fast," assuming that His followers would practice fasting (Matthew 6:16 ASV). Daniel’s example encourages us to set aside seasons for fasting as the Lord leads.
Seeking Understanding and God’s Will
Daniel fasted and prayed for understanding (see Daniel 10:12 ASV), not merely for personal benefit, but to discern God’s purposes. We too are called to seek God’s wisdom:
But if any of you lacketh wisdom, let him ask of God, who giveth to all liberally and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him. - James 1:5 ASV
Humility and Repentance
Daniel’s attitude was one of mourning and humility. True prayer and fasting are often accompanied by repentance and humility before God (2 Chronicles 7:14 ASV).
Applying Daniel’s Example Today
Set Aside Time to Seek God: Like Daniel, we can designate specific times for intentional prayer and fasting, especially in seasons of decision, crisis, or spiritual need.
Pray Persistently: Bring your requests before God with perseverance, trusting Him even when answers are delayed. Remember that spiritual battles may be occurring unseen (Daniel 10:13 ASV).
Incorporate Fasting: As God leads, practice fasting to set aside distractions and focus on seeking Him, whether through food or other means that occupy your heart and mind.
Seek God’s Wisdom, Not Just Your Will: Pray not only for your needs, but for understanding of God’s purposes, submitting your desires to His sovereign will.
Approach God with Humility: Emulate Daniel’s humble posture, recognizing your need for God’s grace and mercy.
Encouragement from God’s Response
God honored Daniel’s pursuit:

Then said he unto me, Fear not, Daniel: for from the first day that thou didst set thy heart to understand, and to humble thyself before thy God, thy words were heard, and I am come for thy words’ sake. - Daniel 10:12 ASV
Even when answers seem delayed, God hears the prayers of those who seek Him with a sincere heart. Through Christ, we have even greater access to God’s throne of grace (Hebrews 4:16 ASV).
